summary.headline: Spencer's Q4 FY26 consolidated sales rose 6% YoY to INR436 crore, with Spencer's format up 8% and first YoY growth in many quarters.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 sales grew 6% YoY to INR436 crore, with EBITDA of INR2 crore against flat last year, and margin at about 18.8%. Spencer's format grew 8% to close to INR380 crore, with H2 growth of almost 4% and month-on-month growth reported since November. Full-year consolidated sales fell about 10% to INR1,800 crore after FY25 store and regional exits, and EBITDA was INR15 crore versus INR60 crore last year, which included one-off other income. Nature's Basket lagged, with management attributing its decline to internal issues such as inventory mix and supply chain problems.

segments.name: Spencer's (offline and online)
segments.commentary: Q4 sales close to INR380 crore, +8% YoY, with online up about 50% and offline up 4.5-5%. FY26 online sales INR200 crore (+37%), with about 2.15 lakh orders per month at INR760 AOV and unit-order breakeven at gross level.

segments.name: Nature's Basket
segments.commentary: Sales declined YoY, with the decline more pronounced in Bangalore and degrowth also in Mumbai. The network has 31 stores; management cites internal issues including excess stock in processed, canned and imported lines and weak fresh availability.

guidance_outlook: Management mandate: achieve operational EBITDA breakeven (including other income, net of interest cash losses zero) within FY27; this is the first milestone before 2-3% EBITDA-positive stage.
Spencer's targets 8% store EBITDA in FY27 (currently about double FY25's low single-digit level); offline business expected to break even in FY27.
Spencer's online loss to be reduced to low double digit, ideally single digit; online revenue targeted at about INR250 crore next year.
Nature's Basket: next two quarters described as critical for returning to growth; no store additions planned.
Interest cost expected to stay in 9.5-10.5% range through FY27; about INR108 crore consolidated debt to be repaid in H1 FY27, with rollover line of sight.
Spencer's to add 3-4 stores in FY27, some new and some relocations; growth mainly from same-store sales.
capex_capacity: Spencer's network of 42 stores plus 1 dark store, covering about 99% of pin codes for online delivery in West Bengal and Kolkata.
Spencer's sales per sq ft rose to about INR1,700 per month from about INR1,400 in FY25; management sees potential of INR2,000.
Nature's Basket operates 31 stores, concentrated in Mumbai and Bangalore; no closures or openings planned, focus on sales per sq ft.
Spencer's online average delivery time about 28.5 minutes against 30-minute proposition; in-full rate close to 90%.
Management stated no equity infusion decision yet; recapitalisation to be evaluated after EBITDA breakeven.
demand_pricing: Spencer's growth driven by ABV growth rather than number of bills in offline; management says NOBs are flat, with ABV rising partly by design through the rewards tiers.
Spencer's offline AOV around INR1,300 (includes liquor); Nature's Basket AOV slightly higher, with no ABV increase seen recently.

Rewards programme (launched July 2025): INR500 annual fee, cash-back up to 6% (INR600 at INR10,000 monthly spend). Close to 100,000 members at year-end; members shop about 4.5x per month vs 2.5x for average customer, spend about INR8,000 per month, and 80%+ N+1 retention; members contribute 20-22% of monthly sales.
Nature's Basket Elysium programme: INR5,000 annual fee for up to 10% off; about 9,000 members, with an internal target of about 30,000. Around 1,250 members added in April.
Online quick-commerce competitors' AOV around INR450-500 vs Spencer's INR760.
Management plans two higher loyalty tiers (Platinum and Diamond) for Spencer's, offering free deliveries and liquor-related rewards.
Nature's Basket is piloting sales through two quick-commerce marketplaces (one in Kolkata, one in Bangalore) with talks with Amazon; management accepts margin dilution from commissions.

qa_highlights.question: Breakout of ABV and number of bills for Spencer's and Nature's Basket.
qa_highlights.answer: Offline breakout not disclosed; growth driven by ABV, with NOBs flat. Online: 2.6 million orders in FY26 (about 2.15 lakh per month) at INR760 AOV.

qa_highlights.question: Debt maturing in H1 FY27 and refinancing plans.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Manjir Basu said about INR108 crore of consolidated debt repays in H1 FY27, requiring refinancing; interest cost expected to remain 9.5-10.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Nature's Basket turnaround measures after the leadership change.
qa_highlights.answer: Priorities: consistent fresh availability (fruits, vegetables, chicken, meat, exotics), rebalancing excess processed, canned and imported stock, rewards expansion, and rebuilt online platform on Jiffy tech stack.

qa_highlights.question: Listing Nature's Basket on quick-commerce platforms.
qa_highlights.answer: Pilot underway with two platforms (Kolkata and Bangalore), with Amazon talks; margin dilution expected but incremental revenue accepted.

qa_highlights.question: Whether Spencer's would also list on marketplaces.
qa_highlights.answer: No; Spencer's online is concentrated in West Bengal and 42 stores plus 1 dark store cover 99% of pin codes; listing would not make EBITDA sense.

qa_highlights.question: Geographic split of Q4 growth and membership accounting.
qa_highlights.answer: Growth secular across East and East UP; East growth mostly online (about 50%), East UP store-led with double-digit growth. Membership cash-back of about INR5.5 crore is booked against net sales and is about 120 bps of margin.

qa_highlights.question: Whether EBITDA breakeven mandate includes other income, and equity infusion plans.
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven includes other income, which is declining; management wants cash losses at zero after interest. Equity infusion to be considered only after breakeven is achieved.

risks_watch: Nature's Basket continues to decline; management expects two critical quarters to show growth and ABV recovery.
Spencer's H1 FY26 was down YoY; sustainability of monthly growth since November 2025 needs tracking.
Online Spencer's EBITDA loss of about INR30 crore in FY26; target reduction depends on scale.
Refinancing of about INR108 crore due in H1 FY27 and reliance on rollover; no equity infusion committed.
Membership cash-back accounting reduces reported gross margin (about 120 bps in Q4 Spencer's); monitor whether this persists.
Possible competitive pressure from quick commerce in Nature's Basket categories, per management's own caveat.
summary.management_tone: Confident about Spencer's recovery and the membership-led growth, while candid that Nature's Basket problems are internal and unresolved. Management was guarded on promoter equity, deadlines and any sale of parts of the business, deferring those to the Board.
key_quotes: This is the first time after many quarters, we've been able to deliver growth over last year.
So clearly, growth is not going to come through massive network expansion.
The mandate to the management team is to do an EBITDA turnaround.
So the real margin delivered on the category intake side is 18.6%.

adds.what: 3-4 Spencer's stores in FY27 (some new, some relocations)

growth.why: Management guides Spencer's online sales from INR200 crore to INR250 crore in FY27 (+25%) and 8% store EBITDA, backed by same-store sales gains (sales/sq ft ~INR1,700 vs INR1,400), loyalty tiers and 3-4 store additions, but no hard capacity or order numbers are given beyond store count; Nature's Basket has no growth plan and no store additions.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management targets 8% store EBITDA in FY27 versus a low single-digit FY25 level, and Spencer's store EBITDA was INR14 crore in Q4 (up about 40% YoY) at a 17.5% margin, though membership cash-back cost about 120 bps and online losses are about INR30 crore for FY26.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Spencer's adds 3-4 stores in FY27, mostly relocations and some new, on a 42-store base (under 10% gross addition), while Nature's Basket has no openings planned across its 31 stores.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Spencer's Q4 sales rose 8% to about INR380 crore with offline up 4.5-5% and online up about 50%, and online revenue is targeted at INR250 crore in FY27 (+25% on INR200 crore), though offline growth is ABV-led with NOBs flat.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed, sales per sq ft rose to about INR1,700 from INR1,400 with potential of INR2,000, and no new plant or line is planned; equity infusion is deferred until after EBITDA breakeven.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Spencer's offline has grown month-on-month since November and H2 grew about 4%, but the company-level breakeven target is still unproven and Nature's Basket is declining.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Nature's Basket sales are falling in Bangalore and Mumbai, management calls the next two quarters critical, and about INR108 crore of debt must be refinanced in H1 FY27 with breakeven still to be reached.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans two higher loyalty tiers (Platinum and Diamond) for Spencer's with free delivery and liquor rewards, and Nature's Basket is piloting quick-commerce listings in Kolkata and Bangalore with Amazon talks underway.

rows.label: Company operational EBITDA breakeven incl. other income in FY27
rows.why: Management's stated mandate for FY27 is operational EBITDA breakeven after interest cash losses, versus FY26 consolidated EBITDA of INR15 crore and a PBT loss of INR250 crore.

rows.label: Refinancing of INR108 crore debt in H1 FY27
rows.why: About INR108 crore of consolidated debt repays in H1 FY27 with rollover line of sight, and interest cost is held at 9.5-10.5%; equity infusion is deferred until after breakeven.

rows.label: Nature's Basket recovery in next two quarters
rows.why: Sales are declining YoY (Bangalore worse, Mumbai also down) across 31 stores with no additions, and management is targeting fresh availability and rebalancing excess processed and imported stock to return to growth.

tone.note: Management was confident on Spencer's membership-led recovery (8% store EBITDA target, sales per sq ft up to about INR1,700) and candid that Nature's Basket problems are internal and unresolved; analysts pressed on ABV versus bill counts, debt refinancing and the sustainability of monthly growth sin
